title: Process Injection: Process Hollowing
summary: Process hollowing creates a legitimate executable in a suspended state, removes its original image from memory, writes attacker code into the freed address space, and resumes the main thread so the payload runs under the identity of a trusted binary. The classic sequence is creation of the process with its primary thread suspended, unmapping of the image section, allocation of new memory in the target, writing of a replacement image, adjustment of the thread context to point at the new entry point, and finally resumption of the thread. Because the suspended process inherits the security context of whatever spawned it, hollowing usually does not raise privilege on its own; its value is disguise and defence evasion. Defenders detect it through behaviour rather than a single signature: a process whose on-disk image does not match its memory image, an image section unmap followed by fresh allocation and resume in the same process, thread start addresses that fall outside every mapped module, and parent-child relationships or command lines that make no sense for the named binary.

beginner.definition: Process hollowing hides malicious code inside a normal program already on the computer. The attacker starts that program but pauses it immediately, before it can do anything. Then the attacker removes the program's real instructions from memory, which is called hollowing. Attacker code fills the empty space, and the program still looks trusted when it continues.
beginner.whyItMatters: Security tools and people trust programs by their names and file paths. In this technique the name is real and the file on disk is genuine. The code running in memory is not the code from that file. That gap between stored files and running code is what you must look for. If you only check file names, you will miss it completely.
howItWorks: The attacker starts a genuine program with a flag that suspends its main thread straight away.
The process now exists, but none of the program's own instructions have run yet.
The attacker unmaps the original image, which removes the program's instructions from memory.
New memory is allocated inside the process, and the attacker's replacement code is written there.
The thread context is changed so the paused thread points at the new entry point.
The thread is resumed, and the disguised process begins running the attacker's hidden payload.
beginner.example: Picture a parcel delivery office on a busy morning. A courier arrives with an official van, an official uniform and a real company badge. The guard waves him through without a second look. What the guard cannot see is that the van left the depot empty. The parcels inside were swapped at the gate. The van is genuine, the uniform is genuine, and the paperwork matches exactly. Only a check of the actual cargo would reveal the change. Process hollowing works the same way, because the outside is real and the contents are not.
takeaways: A trusted file name running does not prove that trusted code is running.
Compare what sits on disk with what is actually loaded in memory.
Hollowing hides code from defences, but it does not usually grant new permissions.

objectives: Explain the suspended process sequence that defines process hollowing.
Describe how hollowing differs from injecting into an already running process.
Identify evidence that a process image in memory does not match its file on disk.
Explain why process hollowing normally does not raise privileges by itself.
List the telemetry sources a defender can use to spot a hollowed process.
